newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity down in retracement of gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity down in retracement of gains.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were lower Friday in a retracement of large gains made through the week, industry sources said.
The gains had come mainly on news of generation outages in the U.S. West, many of which are turning out to be short-term situations, the sources said.
"We seemed to have reached the limit of our bullishness, and a lot of that bullishness was based on short-term factors," said one Houston-based futures trader.

As of 1305 EDT, NYMEX Palo Verde (PV) futures were down $2.25 at $33.45 following exchanges in a range of $33.15-34.25, while August was down $1.20 at $34.60 after trades in a range of $34.50-35.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).

July California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down $1.23 at $21.00 following exchanges in a range of $20.75-21.10, while August was bid at $23.40 and offered at $23.60 following trade down $1.19 at $23.25 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1220 EDT an estimated total of 122 COB and 891 PV contracts traded, of which a significant portion of PV was said to be exchange for physicals.

NYMEX PV futures settled sharply higher Thursday after hitting new contract highs on news of the generation outages in the U.S. West, hot weather in the Southwest and stronger natural gas prices. COB futures also closed stronger on news of California outages and the PV strength.
In power generation, Southern California Edison pushed back the restart of the 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in San Clemente, Calif., to July 10 from late June for additional work.
Also, the 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners, N.M., coal-fired plant may be shut for a week after it tripped off-line Wednesday due to a tube rupture,

Several units which were shut for unexpected maintenance were scheduled to return to service soon, however, including two 750 MW units at the Moss Landing natural gas-fired power plant near Monterey, Calif.
A 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 1 was said to be operating at 615 MW early Friday and was holding at that level following a shutdown Saturday for maintenance.
The 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was tentatively set to restart next Wednesday or Thursday, pending approval from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).

Separately, earlier this week the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) committee recommended a the Pacific Intertie transmission system be derated from July 1-30 to 6,300 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
The plan requires the approval of the WSCC board.
As of 1310 EDT, July Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 2.6 cents at $2.195 per million British thermal units.
Also in natural gas news, the El Paso Natural Gas Co's Blanco gas plant in the San Juan Basin was expected to return to full service soon.

On Friday and Saturday, 240 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas will still be cut, but on Sunday operations at the plant will return to normal. The Blanco plant normally processes about one billion cubic feet per day of gas.

Temperatures through the Pacific Northwest were expected to average near to four degrees Fahreneheit below normal through the weekend, then were expected to moderate to near-normal levels early next week. Unsettled weather was seen through the weekend before conditions were forecast to improve early next week.
In the southwest, the weekend and early next week were expected to be mostly dry and hot with temperatures called to be one to six degrees above normal.
COB open interest for June 19 rose 225 to 7,398, while PV was off 99 at 7,768, NYMEX said.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
